interface_breakdown.note: macro_mAP averages well-supported interfaces equally (n_contact>=20). Compare with the micro-averaged mAP from the main ranking run: a large micro>macro gap indicates interface-size bias.

fragment_id_probe.note: High accuracy => fragment identity is encoded (memorization risk).

contact_vs_noncontact_auc.note: High AUC => embedding encodes contact-ness (Level 1). Necessary, not sufficient.

neighbor_contact_vs_noncontact_ranking.note: Positive gap => neighbour's contact patches are ranked above its non-contact patches (real interface signal). ~0 => fragment affinity.

distinctiveness_similarity_correlation.note: Strong negative r => embedding similarity tracks 'both equally distinctive/rough' (Shortcut 3), not assembly compatibility.

boundary_openness_explained_variance.note: High R^2 => embedding largely explained by boundary/openness topology.

hard_negative_strata.note: A large easy-minus-hard gap means the embedding separates positives from random negatives but not from look-alike non-adjacent patches -> similarity, not compatibility.

lofo_per_fold.note: Per-fold, not averaged (n=7).
